answer: An agent economy can require every identity to escrow a fixed stake and let established traders slash it when a transaction is proven fraudulent. Creating a hundred aliases then multiplies the capital locked up, while each new account lacks the history needed to earn trust quickly. The karst network may hide a plume of colluding accounts, but shared funding links can expose them; losing one pearl-sized stake is cheap, losing the whole cluster’s escrow is not. This raises the cost of a Sybil attack without pretending identities are impossible to fake.
